G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
REGIONAL HEAD
Raghav Khanna
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Manisha, Sales Head  ·  Manages: 5 BMs (1 per branch)

1  ·  Role Purpose
The Regional Head owns end-to-end clinic operations and revenue for a region of five branches. The mandate is two-fold: hold every branch to the GLEUHR standard, and grow region-level revenue and profitability.

In one sentence.  Make every branch in the region operate as well as the best branch in the company — and grow region revenue measurably every quarter.

Reporting structure
Reports to: Manisha (Head of Sales) — for all sales, revenue, conversion, and counsellor-related work
Reports to: Saurabh (Operations Manager) — for all clinic operations, reception, clinical floor, hygiene, audit, and reports
Both Manisha and Saurabh report to the Chief Business Officer (CBO), who reports to the Founder
Manages: 5 Branch Managers (one per branch in the region)
Dotted line to: Head of Clinical (for medical decisions), Head of Marketing (for region-level marketing alignment)
As new branches open in the region, they are added to the Regional Head's portfolio

Two parallel lines, by design.  Sales and operations are different muscles. Manisha holds you accountable for revenue, conversion, follow-ups, upsells. Saurabh holds you accountable for clinic operations, hygiene, audit findings, reports. When the two pull in different directions, the CBO reconciles. This structure is built for scale — it stops a single line from quietly trading operational standard for short-term revenue, or revenue discipline for operational comfort.

2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Five KRAs. Each carries weight in the annual review.
KRA 1 — Branch Operations Quality
Every branch in the region meets the GLEUHR operational standard daily — reception, counsellor, housekeeping, clinical hygiene, treatment delivery
Audit scores from compliance leads are consistently above target across all branches
Client experience metrics (NPS, complaint rate, repeat rate) are above target

KRA 2 — Revenue Ownership
Region revenue meets or exceeds quarterly target
Each branch hits its individual revenue target
Conversion ratios (consult-to-package, package-to-renewal) above target across the region
Active balance recovery — outstanding dues collected before they age

KRA 3 — BM Development
Every BM in the region is performing above standard, or has a documented development plan
Underperforming BMs are coached, escalated, or replaced — not protected
Succession plan exists for every BM — at least one Assistant BM identified per branch
BM attrition in the region is below company average

KRA 4 — Region-Level Execution Discipline
5-day branch cycle followed consistently — twenty to twenty-two days/month in branches
Action plans signed off on Day 1, executed by Day 5 or 6, audited at next visit
Weekly call with Manisha never missed
Monthly business review prepared and presented on time

KRA 5 — Brand Stewardship
Zero brand-damaging incidents in the region — public complaints, regulatory issues, social media flare-ups
Clinical protocols followed across all branches — verified through compliance audits
Any issue surfaced to founder and Sales Head before it reaches public attention

3  ·  Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Specific, measurable, reviewed monthly. Targets to be set within the first 30 days. Sales KPIs set by Manisha; Operations KPIs set by Saurabh. Both reviewed monthly with the Regional Head.

3a  ·  Known Gaps to Fix — to be added after training
This section is intentionally blank at the time the Regional Head receives the document.

Why this is blank.  By the end of the 7-14 day training, the Regional Head will have observed every department at Chandigarh, sat with the online appointments team, read the operations and sales reports, and met with Manisha, Saurabh, and the founder. At that point, the founder and the leadership team will sit down with the Regional Head and document the specific known gaps that need fixing across the region. This list becomes the priority order for the first 90 days in the field. It is added here, in writing, signed by all three (Regional Head, Manisha, Saurabh) before deployment.

Format for this section once filled
Gap 1: [description] — owner: [name] — target close date: [date]
Gap 2: [description] — owner: [name] — target close date: [date]
Gap 3 onwards as needed — typically 5 to 8 priority gaps

4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure — The Branch Cycle
Every branch visit follows this rhythm. Five days minimum, six if execution is not yet smooth. You leave only when execution holds without your interference.
Day 1 — Audit and Action Plan
Morning floor walk with BM. Every department: reception, counsellors, doctors, therapists, housekeeping. Observe, don't correct yet.
Review last 30 days of data: revenue, conversion, NPS, complaints, compliance audit scores, BM scorecards, asks logs.
1-on-1 with BM (60 min): what is working, what is hard, what they need.
Department debriefs (15 min each): hear them directly, not via BM.
End of day: build the 5-day action plan. Three to five priorities. Co-signed by BM. Sent to Manisha + Founder.

Day 2 — Training and Start of Execution
Morning: deliver training on the priority gaps. Departments most affected first.
Mid-day: first wave of execution begins. You are side-by-side with the team, not directing from a desk.
Evening: 30-min review with BM. What worked today, what didn't, what we adjust tomorrow.

Days 3 and 4 — Execution
Full execution. BM leads operationally; you coach in the moment.
By end of Day 4, the team should be running the new standard with minimal interference from you.
Daily 15-min review with BM each evening.
Daily WhatsApp update to Manisha — 5 lines: scores, what improved, what's stuck, ask.

Day 5 (or 6) — Handover
Handover happens only when execution is stable without your interference. Not before.
Lock the 30/60/90-day commitments with BM. Written. Co-signed.
Set the next visit date.
Final report to Manisha + Founder: branch state, what changed, what is still open, when you return.
Leave.

The handover principle.  If execution falters the moment you leave, the visit failed. Stay an extra day. Better to leave one branch later than to leave five branches running on your shadow.

6  ·  Authority and Escalation
What the Regional Head decides without escalation
Branch-level operational decisions, day-to-day discipline of BMs
Action plans for each branch within the agreed strategy
Training schedules within the region
Day-to-day spend within the regional budget
Branch-level scheduling, leaves, and team logistics

What needs Manisha's sign-off (Sales line)
Hiring or terminating a BM (revenue-side authority)
Revenue target changes mid-quarter
Sales budget variance beyond agreed threshold
Sales compensation changes for team in region
Marketing or lead-generation strategy changes

What needs Saurabh's sign-off (Operations line)
Hiring or terminating a BM (operations-side authority — must align with Manisha)
Major operational changes affecting more than one branch
Vendor and supplier decisions affecting branches
Operations budget variance beyond agreed threshold
Audit finding resolution that requires capital expenditure

What needs CBO's sign-off
Disagreement between Manisha and Saurabh that affects your region
Strategy changes that span both sales and operations
Region-level resourcing decisions (additional headcount, structural changes)

What comes to the Founder
Serious client complaint with reputational risk
Regulatory or legal issue
Public relations incident
Loss of a key senior person (BM, senior doctor, senior counsellor)
Disagreement between Manisha and Saurabh that the CBO has not resolved within a reasonable window

Speed of escalation.  An issue that needs founder attention should reach the founder the same day, not at the next monthly review. Speed is the signal of seriousness.

7  ·  Don'ts
Behaviours that are not acceptable, regardless of revenue performance.

Protecting a BM who is failing because of personal loyalty or comfort
Having favourites — a 'preferred' branch that gets more attention or softer reviews
Hiding problems from Manisha or Founder — the company can only fix what it knows about
Correcting things you do not fully understand — especially clinical or hygiene matters; consult the clinical lead first
Bypassing the BM to instruct their team directly without telling them
Using authority to settle interpersonal issues; use it to set the standard
Treating company decisions as suggestions
Promising clients or BMs anything that has not been agreed with Manisha

8  ·  Consequences Framework
Performance management is graduated and documented. Final consequences in line with HR policy.
Trigger
Response
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with Manisha; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months miss
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR involvement
Single-incident breach of a Don't (e.g. hiding a problem, bypassing BM)
Written warning on first occurrence — zero tolerance
Repeated policy breach
Termination consideration
Serious dishonesty with Founder or Manisha
Single-incident termination consideration

9  ·  First 90 Days — Probation
The first 90 days are a structured probation period.

Phase 1 — Days 1 to 14: Training
7-14 days at Chandigarh HQ. Length depends on training completion.
Trained on every department — reception, counsellors, doctors, therapists, housekeeping, hygiene, sales operations.
Sign-off by all trainers required before field deployment.
Manisha + Founder meeting at end of training to deploy formally.

Phase 2 — Days 15 to 45: First branch cycles, supervised
First two branch visits done alongside Manisha or a senior trainer for the first 1-2 days each.
Daily WhatsApp to Manisha during first cycles.
Mid-phase review at Day 30.

Phase 3 — Days 46 to 90: Independent operation
Solo branch cycles. Full ownership.
Weekly 30-min call with Manisha.
End of Day 90: confirmation review with Manisha + Founder. Probation closed if KPIs trending positive and no Don'ts breached.

Probation can close early.  If by Day 60 you are clearly delivering and the BMs are responding positively, probation can be closed early at Manisha's recommendation.

10  ·  What 'Done' Looks Like — End of First Year

Every branch in the region is delivering against its revenue target.
Compliance audit scores are consistently at standard, no branch persistently below.
BM team is stable, developing, and has documented succession plans.
NPS / client feedback in the region is above company average.
Founder and Manisha can leave the region alone for 30 days without anything breaking.

The ultimate test.  When the founder visits a branch unannounced and finds it running well — not better than usual, just normally well — the Regional Head has done their job. Excellence shown when no one is watching is the only excellence that counts.
